check.population: every multi-step write, shared mutable state and retried side effect
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the write path, the isolation level or the concurrency model changes
check.refusal: the transaction or concurrency test fails a write path that loses an update, commits partially or repeats an effect
check.observation: outcomes of concurrent and retried runs, plus the transaction boundaries read from source
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the transaction boundary and the isolation level, which every write path conforms to

records.name: Idempotency
records.definition: A design rule that repeating an operation with the same input has the same effect as running it once.

records.name: Atomicity
records.definition: A design rule that the steps of a state change either all take effect or none do.

exemplar.before:
await fooStore.remove(from, foo.id);
await fooStore.add(to, foo.id);

distinctFrom.reason: ACID keeps each transaction atomic, consistent, isolated and durable, while BASE favors availability and lets replicas converge later.

records.name: ACID
records.definition: A conceptual representation of the four guarantees of a database transaction: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

distinctFrom.reason: A transaction boundary fixes which writes one transaction covers, while consistency rules are the invariants it must keep inside that scope.

records.name: Transaction Boundary
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a transaction covers exactly the writes of one unit of work inside one service.

records.name: Unit of Work Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that collects the changes of one use case and commits them together in a single transaction.
detected_by: multiple independent saves in one use case

distinctFrom.reason: Consistency is stored data satisfying its invariants, while correctness is code behavior matching its specification.
Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while fault tolerance is operation continuing through component failure.
Consistency is data inside one system keeping its invariants, while interoperability is separate systems exchanging data.
Consistency is invariants holding after every change, while always-fresh reads is every read seeing the latest write.
Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while availability is the system answering at all.
Consistency is invariants holding after a change, while durability is a committed change surviving a crash.
Consistency is a property of stored data, while maintainability is a property of the code that changes it.
Consistency is invariants holding, while scalability is performance holding as load grows.
Consistency is invariants holding, while operational complexity is the effort of running the system in production.
Consistency is one property of stored data, while quality is how far a system meets all its expectations.
Consistency is data keeping its invariants, while security is protection from misuse and attack.
Consistency is invariants holding, while simplicity is the absence of unneeded structure.

records.name: Consistency
records.definition: The degree to which stored data satisfies its invariants after every change.

exemplar.before:
foo.total = foo.items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.value, 0);
foo.itemCount = externalCount;

records.name: Isolation
records.definition: A rule or precondition that concurrent transactions do not see each other's uncommitted changes, to the degree the isolation level declares.

records.name: Concurrency Control
records.definition: A mechanism that coordinates concurrent access to shared state, through locks, versions or compare-and-swap.

exemplar.before:
const foo = await fooStore.find(id);
await fooStore.save({ ...foo, count: foo.count + 1 });

records.name: Optimistic Locking
records.definition: A design pattern that checks a record's version when it is written and rejects the write if another writer changed it first, comparing only the writer's own span where a surface is fenced per writer.

exemplar.before: await fooTable.update({ id: foo.id, name: foo.name });

records.name: Pessimistic Locking
records.definition: A design pattern that locks a record before reading it for update, so other writers wait until the transaction ends.

exemplar.before:
const foo = await fooTable.find(id);
await fooTable.save(change(foo));

records.name: State Isolation
records.definition: A design rule that each piece of mutable state belongs to one unit of concurrent execution, so no two units that run at the same time can write it.

exemplar.before:
const globalFooState: Foo[] = [];
function addFoo(foo: Foo) { globalFooState.push(foo); }

records.name: Controlled Side Effects
records.definition: A design rule that mutation, I/O and persistence happen at declared boundaries, around a core of pure functions.

records.name: Petri Nets
records.definition: A conceptual representation of concurrent flow as places holding tokens and transitions that consume and produce them, which can be analyzed for deadlock.
detected_by: deadlocks or lost tokens found only at runtime
